title: Management of Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF)
summary: HFpEF management focuses on symptom relief, decongestion, cardiorenal protection, and reduction of HF hospitalizations with SGLT2 inhibitors as foundational therapy. Add-on therapies target comorbidities and phenotypes (hypertension, AF, obesity, CKD, pulmonary hypertension), with careful diuretic titration and exercise training to improve quality of life.

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Heart Failure Regardless of Diabetes
summary: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart failure hospitalizations and cardiovascular death across the EF spectrum independent of diabetes. Benefits emerge within weeks, with consistent safety signals and modest eGFR dip. Incorporate dapagliflozin or empagliflozin as foundational therapy for HFrEF and as additive therapy for HFmrEF/HFpEF.

title: Hypertension Management: Contemporary Guideline Updates and Therapeutic Sequencing
summary: Current guidance emphasizes accurate diagnosis with out-of-office monitoring, earlier combination therapy, and aggressive cardiovascular risk reduction. First-line agents remain thiazide-like diuretics, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, and calcium-channel blockers, with beta-blockers reserved for specific indications. Target <130/80 mmHg for most high-risk adults; use single-pill combinations to improve adherence. SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 RAs reduce CV events in diabetes and CKD and are complementary to BP therapy.

title: Rate vs Rhythm Control in 2025: Contemporary Strategy and Evidence
summary: Early rhythm control using antiarrhythmics and/or catheter ablation reduces cardiovascular events compared with rate control in selected patients, while lenient rate control remains acceptable for symptom-driven care. Decisions hinge on symptom burden, heart failure status, comorbidities, and time since AF diagnosis. Anticoagulation is guided by stroke risk, independent of strategy.

title: Practical, Evidence-Based Management of Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF)
summary: HFpEF care centers on aggressive comorbidity control and proven cardioprotective therapies. SGLT2 inhibitors reduce HF events regardless of diabetes status, MRAs and ARNI offer selective benefit, and GLP-1 RAs show promise in obese HFpEF. Tailor diuretics, optimize blood pressure and rhythm, and target obesity, AF, pulmonary hypertension, and CKD to improve outcomes.

title: Atrial Fibrillation: Rate vs Rhythm Control in 2025
summary: Contemporary evidence favors early rhythm control—especially with catheter ablation—for symptom control and reduction of cardiovascular events in selected patients, while rate control remains appropriate for many with minimal symptoms or advanced comorbidity. Trials such as EAST-AFNET 4, CASTLE-AF, and CABANA clarify who benefits most, and real-world data support early adoption with careful patient selection.

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors in Heart Failure—Benefits Independent of Diabetes
summary: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart failure events and mortality across the LVEF spectrum regardless of diabetes. Benefits are rapid, additive to guideline-directed therapy, and accompanied by improved health status and renal protection. Initiate in most ambulatory and hospitalized patients unless contraindicated.

title: Evaluation and Management of Chest Pain in the Emergency Department
summary: Rapid, risk-stratified evaluation with high-sensitivity troponin, ECG, and clinical gestalt safely identifies low-risk patients for early discharge while expediting definitive care for ACS. Contemporary trials support 0/1‑hour and 0/2‑hour hs‑cTn algorithms, selective imaging, and guideline-directed antithrombotic therapy.

title: Approach to Elevated Troponin and Non‑Ischemic Myocardial Injury
summary: Elevated troponin indicates myocardial injury, not etiology. Distinguish acute myocardial infarction (MI) from acute/chronic non‑ischemic injury using symptoms, ECG, serial high‑sensitivity assays, and imaging. Management targets the cause (e.g., tachyarrhythmia, sepsis, myocarditis) rather than universal ACS therapy, which may harm when ischemia is absent.

title: Hypertension Management: Current Guideline Updates and Therapeutic Sequencing
summary: Contemporary guidance emphasizes accurate diagnosis, earlier combination therapy, and outcome‑driven sequencing anchored in compelling indications. High‑quality trials support thiazide‑like diuretics, ACEi/ARB, and CCB as first‑line; beta‑blockers are reserved for specific indications. SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP‑1 RAs confer BP‑lowering and CV–renal benefit in comorbid diabetes/HF. Resistant hypertension requires structured evaluation, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, and consideration of device therapy.

title: Perioperative Management of Patients With Coronary Stents
summary: Time-sensitive surgery after PCI requires balancing stent thrombosis risk against bleeding. Prioritize delaying elective surgery, continuing aspirin, and tailoring P2Y12 interruption/resumption based on stent type, time from PCI, and procedural bleeding risk, with bridging only in select very high thrombotic risk cases.

title: Rate vs Rhythm Control in Atrial Fibrillation: Contemporary Strategy in 2025
summary: Early rhythm control—especially with catheter ablation—improves hard outcomes in newly diagnosed AF with cardiovascular comorbidity, while strict rate control remains acceptable for minimally symptomatic patients. Evidence favors rhythm control for reducing cardiovascular events, HF hospitalizations, and progression to persistent AF, with the greatest benefit when initiated early.

title: Contemporary Management of Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF)
summary: HFpEF care centers on guideline-directed pharmacotherapy (SGLT2 inhibitors for all, diuretics for congestion, selected use of MRA and ARNI), rigorous comorbidity control (BP, AF, obesity, diabetes, CKD, pulmonary hypertension), and lifestyle/rehab. SGLT2 inhibitors consistently reduce HF hospitalization and improve quality of life; ARNI and MRA offer selective benefits in phenotypes with elevated natriuretic peptides or LVEF below the upper range. Tailor therapy to hemodynamics and phenotype, and monitor renal function and potassium closely.

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors for Heart Failure Regardless of Diabetes Status
summary: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce heart failure events and improve health status across HFrEF and HFpEF, independent of diabetes. Benefits emerge within weeks, with consistent safety and modest eGFR dip. Initiate in stable outpatients or during/after hospitalization, alongside guideline-directed therapy.

title: Approach to Syncope: Bedside Diagnosis and Risk Stratification
summary: Syncope evaluation begins with targeted history, physical exam, and a 12‑lead ECG—these alone establish a cause in many patients and determine short‑term risk. Use validated tools cautiously; clinician gestalt plus red flags outperform any single score. Admit or closely monitor patients with high‑risk features; otherwise, discharge with prompt follow‑up and selective testing.

title: Lipid Management in Secondary Prevention: Beyond Statins
summary: In very-high-risk ASCVD, intensify beyond maximally tolerated statins to achieve LDL-C <55 mg/dL (or ≥50% reduction). Add ezetimibe first, then PCSK9 inhibitor or inclisiran; consider bempedoic acid if statin-intolerant. Evidence shows larger absolute benefits at lower LDL-C with acceptable safety.

title: Myocarditis and Pericarditis After Viral Infection or Vaccination
summary: Myocarditis/pericarditis risk is substantially higher after acute SARS-CoV-2 infection than after mRNA vaccination, though myocarditis occurs rarely post-vaccine—primarily in adolescent/young adult males after dose 2 or bivalent boosters. Most vaccine-associated cases are mild and resolve with NSAIDs/rest; infection-associated cases carry higher arrhythmic and heart failure risk. Contemporary population studies and active surveillance affirm a favorable benefit–risk profile for vaccination.

title: Early Inpatient Management of Acute Pulmonary Embolism
summary: Rapid risk stratification, prompt anticoagulation, and selective escalation to thrombolysis or catheter-based therapy reduce early mortality and decompensation in acute PE. Use PESI/sPESI plus imaging/biomarkers to classify risk, initiate anticoagulation within hours, and reserve advanced reperfusion for high-risk or deteriorating intermediate-high–risk patients.
